title: bob-navigation-hotkeys: plain scheduled-property picker write doesn't thread picker baseDate as today for Blocked marking
close_reason: Let's let this slide for now.
description:
In BulletPropertyPickerModal.applySelectedValue (plugins/bob-navigation-hotkeys/main.js, bob-plugins repo), the generic (non-priority, non-project-frontmatter) branch calls this.plugin.setBulletPropertyValue(...) without a `today` option:

    return await this.plugin.setBulletPropertyValue(
      this.editor,
      this.cursor,
      this.selectedPropertyItem.property.name,
      item.value,
      {
        filePath: this.filePath,
        expectedLine: this.lineText,
        scheduleLog: options.scheduleLog,
      },
    );

setBulletPropertyValue forwards to setInlineBulletPropertyValues, whose blocking check falls back to `options.today instanceof Date ? ... : new Date()` -- i.e. real wall-clock time -- when deciding whether a chosen `scheduled` date is "future" and should mark the task Blocked ([?]).

This is inconsistent with the priority-level write path (setBulletPriorityValue), which explicitly threads `baseDate: this.valueBaseDate` through as `today` so Blocked-marking is reproducible relative to the picker's own fixed base date, not the real clock.

Effect: picking a plain scheduled date (including the pinned priority-roll suggestion row in the `scheduled` value stage, which also goes through this generic branch) produces Blocked-marking that silently depends on when the code actually runs, not on the picker's `valueBaseDate`. A fixture asserting a specific Blocked/[?'] vs unblocked/[ ] outcome for this path will start failing (or silently stop covering the intended case) as real time passes the fixture's hardcoded dates.

Found while implementing bob-cli's plan sase/repos/plans/202608/auto_schedule_reasons.md (deterministic schedule-log reasons for machine-rolled dates). A new test for the pinned priority-roll suggestion ("choosing a priority roll writes immediately with a deterministic reason instead of prompting", scripts/test-navigation-hotkeys.cjs) had to read the actual checkbox status at runtime via helpers.getObsidianTaskCheckboxStatus() instead of asserting a hardcoded [?'] or [ ], specifically to route around this wall-clock dependency -- the plan's own worked example assumed [?'] but the assertion only holds if the test happens to run before the rolled date, which is not guaranteed.

Suggested fix: thread `today: this.valueBaseDate` (falling back to a fresh Date the way the priority path already does) through applySelectedValue's generic property branch, matching the priority branch's existing pattern.

title: Future-Pomodoro-link cleanup leaves a dangling trailing newline when the pruned bullet is the file's last line
description:
Discovered while implementing the plan activate_future_scheduled_pomodoro_links.md
(bob-plugins repo, plugins/block-id-prompt/main.js).

listItemSubtreeEdit() (used by planFuturePomodoroLinkCleanup(), called from
completeTaskSourceLink() to prune duplicate future-Pomodoro links) computes the removed
span as [start-of-removed-line, start-of-next-line-or-content.length). This correctly
merges surrounding content when the removed bullet is in the middle of the file, but
when the removed bullet IS the file's last line (no trailing newline after it), the
newline that separated it from the PREVIOUS line is left untouched and nothing follows
to reconnect to, so the file gains a trailing newline it never had.

Repro: a note ending in (no trailing newline)
  - [ ] Later ()
    - [[Alpha#^ship]]
where "[[Alpha#^ship]]" is a dedicated duplicate-link bullet that
planFuturePomodoroLinkCleanup prunes as part of completing a task-picker link elsewhere
in the same Pomodoros section. After pruning, the file ends with
"- [ ] Later ()\n" instead of "- [ ] Later ()" — an unwanted trailing newline introduced
by the cleanup edit.

I worked around this in my own new tests (scripts/test-block-id-prompt.cjs) by ensuring
the pruned bullet is never literally the last line of the fixture, so it did not block
the plan I was implementing. The same subtree-removal shape may exist elsewhere in this
monorepo (e.g. bob-navigation-hotkeys/main.js shares similar list-subtree-removal
helpers) — worth checking during triage whether the same bug is present there too.

title: Persist the Bob Mac Capture retained live draft across restarts
description:
## Feature proposal

Persist the Bob Mac Capture retained live draft so Escape / failed-capture text survives Quit, Restart, crash, and logout.

After https://github.com/bobs-org/bob-mac-capture/pull/1, Control-C canceled drafts write through to `~/Library/Application Support/org.bobs.bob-mac-capture/canceled-draft-stash.json`. The in-editor live draft does not. `CapturePanelModel` still keeps it only in memory (`attributedDraft` / `plainDraft`, plus presentation state such as `errorMessage` and `statusText`). `prepareForRetainedClose()` / `closeRetainingDraft()` set `"Draft retained"` and dismiss the panel; `prepareForPresentation()` reopens that in-memory draft on the next hotkey. `AppDelegate` constructs a fresh `CapturePanelModel` on every launch, so the retained draft is gone after any process exit.

This is a different store from the canceled-draft stash: one current draft (not a bounded newest-first list), restored automatically on next panel open rather than through Control-S, and discarded by **Discard** / Control-C / successful capture rather than by Clear Stash. The approved persist-stash plan named this as out of scope and asked for a follow-up task bead rather than folding it into that PR.

### Evidence

- `Sources/BobMacCapture/CapturePanelModel.swift` — `prepareForRetainedClose()`, `closeRetainingDraft()`, `prepareForPresentation()`, and `discardDraft()` operate only on in-memory published state. There is no encode, decode, or file I/O.
- Tests `testEscapeClosesOnceAndRetainsNonemptyDraft` and `testEscapeDismissesCompletionBeforeClosingPanel` assert in-process retention only.
- PR-branch README Privacy still says captured text lives only in the panel's in-memory draft (plus the new on-disk stash for Control-C). A live-draft persist would be a second documented-guarantee change, same class of README/Settings rewrite the stash work required.

### Suggested shape (not a plan)

Mirror the stash store: Foundation-only CaptureCore JSON file under the same 0700 Application Support directory, write-through on retain/discard/success, delete the file when the live draft is empty, metadata-only errors, never interpolate draft text. Do not persist completion candidates, preview payloads, or diagnostics that are not needed to reopen the editor exactly as left. Confirm with the owner whether a failed capture's `errorMessage` should survive relaunch.

Work is in the `bob-mac-capture` linked repo. Linux can type-check CaptureCore only; macOS CI is the real gate.

Plan that scoped this out: `plan:202608/persist_canceled_draft_stash.md`.
